title: Introducing Thumb Command: Save Planet Earth
description: Meet the Blueguard interceptor, the cities it protects, and the worldwide fight at the heart of Four of Hearts Interactive’s new arcade-defense direction.
imageAlt: Blueguard interceptor defending Chicago from a purple alien invasion

body.heading: A new command for Planet Earth
paragraphs: Thumb Command is a new creative direction from Four of Hearts Interactive: a fast, colorful arcade-defense game built around one clear promise—save Planet Earth.

Alien forces are descending on the cities below. The player launches the blue-white-gold Blueguard interceptor, breaks incoming formations, protects the city shield, and keeps every projectile away from the people beneath the battle.

body.heading: The city is the base
paragraphs: There is no expendable outpost. Chicago, San Francisco, New York City, London, Tokyo, and future campaign destinations are the bases. Their skylines, weather, shields, and attack patterns give each defense a different pulse.
Thumb Command is in development. No public build, platform release, or release date has been announced; future availability news will be published only when it is real.

title: The City Is the Base: Building Thumb Command’s New Battlefields
description: Why Chicago sits directly beneath the player—and how five cities turn shield defense into a worldwide arcade campaign.
imageAlt: Thumb Command battle above Chicago with the city shield active

body.heading: Start at the lakefront
paragraphs: Chicago is the first flagship battlefield because its skyline makes the stakes immediately readable. The Blueguard occupies the air above the lakefront while incoming ships and projectiles press toward the city shield.

Putting the city directly beneath the player changes the feeling of every missed shot. Shield condition and city damage are not abstract meters; they describe the place the player can see and is fighting to protect.

body.heading: A city campaign with a new sky every time
paragraphs: San Francisco catches the invasion at sunset. New York fights through rain and lightning. London protects the Thames under a gold shield. Tokyo becomes a neon counterstrike as portals open above the city.
The shared mission stays clear while atmosphere, visibility, enemy rhythm, and shield color make every stop feel like a new defense—not a recycled background.

title: Meet the Blueguard: Earth’s Last Interceptor
description: Inside Thumb Command’s blue-white-gold hero ship, responsive arcade control, and Vanguard, Sentinel, and Paladin upgrade path.
imageAlt: Blueguard interceptor and its Vanguard, Sentinel, and Paladin upgrade forms

body.heading: Built for speed and clarity
paragraphs: The Blueguard’s royal blue, white, cyan, and gold silhouette is designed to stay readable against deep space, bright shields, city lights, and dense enemy formations.

Responsive movement keeps the ship connected to the player’s thumb while its weapon rhythm lets positioning remain the main decision. Speed, attack spread, shields, missiles, and repairs deepen the run without burying the arcade action.

body.heading: Vanguard. Sentinel. Paladin.
paragraphs: Vanguard is the first major refit, sharpening the Blueguard for a faster offensive push. Sentinel reinforces defensive systems for longer waves. Paladin is the ship at full authority: broader, brighter, and equipped for the largest boss formations.
Purple and magenta alien technology creates an instant visual contrast. Even at the most crowded moment, the player should know which ship is theirs and where safety lies.

title: Designing the Alien Invasion of Thumb Command
description: How purple silhouettes, readable formations, distinct enemy classes, and a massive Mothership create family-friendly arcade pressure.
imageAlt: Purple and magenta Mothership boss from Thumb Command

body.heading: A fleet you can read at full speed
paragraphs: The alien identity begins with dark purple armor, magenta energy, coral highlights, and silhouettes that remain distinct in motion. Stingrays dart through gaps, Voidrippers pressure the edges, Hexblades hold dangerous lanes, and Skitterers, Wraiths, and Bloodbites change the shape of a wave.
Formations communicate risk before they fire. That visual clarity lets the screen become spectacular without turning the game into noise.

body.heading: The Mothership changes the scale
paragraphs: Boss encounters bring the Mothership close enough to dominate the sky. Its glowing core, armored wings, and supporting fleet make the threat feel enormous while the Blueguard remains precise and hopeful at the center of the defense.
The excitement stays family-friendly: bright projectiles, shields, energy bursts, and mechanical alien craft create danger without graphic violence.

title: From Chicago to Tokyo: The Thumb Command World Tour
description: Five cities establish a worldwide campaign—and a flexible foundation for future Thumb Command missions.
imageAlt: San Francisco, New York City, London, and Tokyo campaign environments from Thumb Command

body.heading: Protect the whole planet
paragraphs: Thumb Command begins with recognizable places because the mission is planetary, not distant. Chicago’s lakefront, San Francisco’s bay, New York’s harbor, London’s Thames, and Tokyo’s neon skyline make every victory feel connected to Earth.
The Blueguard and alien fleet remain consistent, but the environment changes the color, weather, rhythm, and emotional temperature of the fight.

body.heading: A campaign designed to expand
paragraphs: The city-as-base structure gives future missions a clear foundation: a place worth protecting, a shield under pressure, and an invasion pattern shaped for that skyline.
No additional city, launch window, or public platform is being promised here. The city campaign describes the current creative direction and the room it leaves for future development.

title: Bobby the Breadasaurus Builds a Tower Defense
description: Bobby’s current direction puts the little dinosaur at the centre of a colourful bread-powered tower-defense game.

body.heading: A small hero holds a very busy path
paragraphs: Four of Hearts Interactive is developing Bobby the Breadasaurus: Tower Defense Adventures, a bright strategy game about placing bread-powered towers, reading incoming routes, and protecting the Breadstone.
The project is in internal development. Current artwork and systems establish direction, not a promise about final platforms, features, or release timing.

body.heading: Build, upgrade, and move Bobby
paragraphs: Toast Zappers, Knife Blocks, Crumb Blasters, and Flour Storm towers make the battlefield readable and playful while Bobby’s own movement gives the player a heroic decision beyond tower placement.
The warmer tower-defense identity replaces the earlier public platform-adventure framing.

title: Evil Doom Girl Adventures Enters Dual-Hero Development
description: Evil Doom Boy and Evil Doom Girl share one action-adventure identity built around movement, trust, and rescue.

body.heading: Two shadows. One adventure.
paragraphs: Evil Doom Girl Adventures is a dual-hero action game in development at Four of Hearts Interactive. Evil Doom Boy and Evil Doom Girl trade the lead through a rescue mission that keeps testing whether they can trust each other.
Current visual and movement explorations are development directions rather than a claim that a public build exists.

body.heading: A distinct visual language
paragraphs: Evil Doom Boy moves through black, charcoal, and dangerous red. Evil Doom Girl's approved website identity uses deep purple, anchored by #4E2A84, to stay fierce and distinct without leaning on hot pink.
No release date, public platform, level count, rating, or public availability has been announced.

title: Why We're Building Palace
description: A familiar card-table game deserves a modern home that respects its mystery, momentum, and many table traditions.
imageAlt: Palace castle artwork from Four of Hearts Interactive

body.heading: The game people teach from memory
paragraphs: Palace often arrives without a box or a manual. Someone at the table remembers the three layers, deals the cards, and teaches the next person by playing a hand. That passed-along quality is part of its charm.

It is easy to begin: match or climb, pick up when the table turns against you, and work through your hand, visible reserve, and hidden finale. The decisions become memorable because every card you save changes the shape of the ending.

body.heading: A definitive modern experience
paragraphs: Four of Hearts Interactive is building Palace as its flagship experience. Our aim is clear presentation, welcoming teaching, responsive play, and a table that feels lively without losing the human rhythm of the folk game.

Founder testing is underway. Palace is not publicly available in an app store yet, and we will not pretend otherwise. Development news will stay honest about what has been tested and what is still ahead.

title: Palace Enters Founder Testing
description: The flagship Four of Hearts experience is in hands-on internal testing, with attention on clarity, feel, and the full table journey.

body.heading: Testing the whole journey
paragraphs: Founder testing is focused on the moments that make Palace feel like Palace: reading the pile, choosing when to spend a strong card, moving from the hand to the face-up reserve, and trusting the final hidden cards.

Internal Alpha means the experience is still changing. Visual feedback, reconnect behavior, scoring, accessibility, and table clarity all require careful testing before any public release claim would be appropriate.

body.heading: What visitors can try now
paragraphs: The website includes a short, self-contained teaching preview. It runs entirely in the browser, stores nothing, and is not a production match. Its job is to make the three-layer rhythm understandable in about a minute.

The website preview now teaches the approved Four of Hearts power cards in context: 2 resets, 7 requires lower, 8 is transparent, and 10 burns the pile. These product rules are not presented as universal folk-game rules.

title: What We’re Making at 4OH
description: A direct look at the current Four of Hearts lineup, from classic cards to arcade defense, puzzle play, and new experiments.
imageAlt: Four of Hearts brand board with Palace, Hearts, Spades, and Euchre

body.heading: The current lineup
paragraphs: Palace is the playable card-table preview. Thumb Command brings colorful arcade defense. Bobby brings tower defence; Evil Doom Girl Adventures brings a dual-hero rescue; HeartStack, Princess Land, and Unicorn Land bring puzzle and creative play.
Hearts, Spades, and Euchre round out the current lineup with three kinds of classic card-table strategy.

body.heading: Still in testing
paragraphs: Every title is still being built or tested. Website lessons demonstrate real ideas from the card games, but they are not complete public releases. Bobby, Evil Doom Girl Adventures, and Thumb Command do not have public builds or announced release dates.
The lineup can grow without turning the studio into a grand theory. We will introduce more only when there is an approved product and an honest status to share.

title: Building a Safer, Family-Friendly Card Table
description: How Four of Hearts approaches clear policies, restrained data use, accessibility, and honest Internal Alpha communication.

body.heading: Trust starts with plain language
paragraphs: A family-friendly game company should explain what is available, what is being tested, and what information may be involved. Our public pages distinguish the static website from Internal Alpha game services and avoid promises the current product cannot support.
The website has no analytics, advertising, account system, form backend, cookie, tracking pixel, or social widget. Its tutorials keep progress only in page memory.

body.heading: Safety is ongoing work
paragraphs: Accessibility, security, privacy, reconnect behavior, rankings, operational logs, and support processes all require review as the games evolve. Our policies describe current limitations and identify the questions that must be revisited before a wider release.
Security reports and player-support requests currently use support@4ohi.com. We do not promise a bug bounty or a guaranteed response time.

title: Welcome to the Four of Hearts Studio
description: Meet the independent South Dakota software studio making classic cards, original games, and useful applications.

body.heading: Small studio. Plenty in progress.
paragraphs: Four of Hearts Interactive, LLC is a South Dakota software studio creating original card, arcade, strategy, platform, puzzle, and creative experiences.
We like old games. We like new games. Mostly, we like making things that are easy to begin and worth coming back to.

body.heading: A public home for the work
paragraphs: This newsroom will document meaningful milestones, teaching decisions, safety work, and product stories. We will not manufacture launch dates, player counts, reviews, or partnerships.
If you are helping test a Four of Hearts game, the Support page explains how to send a useful report to support@4ohi.com.
